==Ingredients==
*6 [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]
*1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
*3 cups water
*2 cubes [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|chicken bouillon]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] to taste
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Flour|all-purpose flour]]
*1 tbsp dried [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
*¼ tsp dried [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]

==Procedure==
#Cook onion in butter until tender.
#Bring the diced potatoes, carrots, water and chicken bouillon in another stock pot to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] about 10 minutes or until tender. Add ground black pepper.
#Add the flour to the cooked onions to make a paste. Stir in the milk. Cook over low heat stirring constantly until warmed through. Add the potato and carrot mixture. Stir in the parsley and thyme and heat through. Serve hot.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*Use vegetable [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]] instead of chicken bouillon for a vegetarian soup.
*Add [[Cookbook:Leek|leeks]] if available.
*Omit all ingredients except potatoes, water, salt and pepper for a simple and surprisingly pleasing potato soup. High quality, flavorful potatoes are required for this variation, which itself presents an ideal base for an inventive cook to expand upon.
